subject: Aligning on 3-year prepay billing cadence & revenue recognition for FT-2312
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@fintrust.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prepay billing — need split invoicing & revrec confirmation

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the call this morning. FinTrust is very interested in the 3-year committed prepay (we're targeting 36 months / $1.2M commit under FT-2312) but our procurement and finance teams need two things clarified before we proceed:

1) Can Redwood issue invoices split by our fiscal years (we close FY on 06/30) rather than a single upfront invoice? Our controller needs the spend to be allocated to FY26/FY27/FY28 budgets.
2) How will Redwood recognize revenue for a multi-year prepay? We need auditor-friendly language confirming that invoicing cadence does not alter ASC 606 treatment (we'll need a memo or summary for our audit team).

If you can loop in your finance lead and sales ops, we can share a PO and preferred billing addresses. Attached is our standard procurement template (see referenced attachment — procurement_form.pdf).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jordan

Jordan Mills
Procurement Manager
FinTrust Corp

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@fintrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prepay billing — need split invoicing & revrec confirmation

Jordan —

Thanks, and great question. Looping in Karthik (finance) and Neha (sales ops) to confirm the options and provide the audit memo. High-level, there are two ways we typically handle multi-year prepay billing while keeping your internal budgeting happy:

Option A — Upfront full prepay (preferred for pricing): Redwood invoices the full committed amount at signing and recognizes revenue ratably over the 36-month service period. We can provide three "allocation" invoices (one per FY) for your internal AP to match budgets; on our side the cash hit is upfront and we book deferred revenue. This preserves the deepest term discount (we offer an extra 6% for full upfront prepay vs annual billing).

Option B — Contractual annual prepay with committed schedule: The contract includes a 3x annual invoice schedule (each invoice due on the contract anniversary) and a slightly smaller term discount (typical: +3% vs pay-as-you-go). Redwood treats each prepaid tranche as deferred revenue that is recognized over the corresponding 12-month coverage window.

Practical implications:
- The invoicing shape (split invoices vs single) does not change ASC 606 revenue recognition — recognition follows the service period.
- For audit evidence, we can provide a short revrec memo and a sample journal entry mapping (deferred revenue -> monthly recognized revenue) plus a copy of the signed contract showing committed amounts.

I'll attach a proposed billing schedule that maps the $1.2M commit into three FY allocations (for Option A) and a quick revrec one-pager. Next steps: if Option A is acceptable, we can generate three allocation invoices with a single DocuSign signature and a single payment instruction, or, if you need separate POs per FY, we can set up one contract with three invoices.

Proposed next step: 30-min call with Karthik + your controller to confirm PO/GL details and finalize the billing cadence. Available tomorrow 11–1pm PT — does that work?

Best,

Dylan Brooks
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@fintrust.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prepay billing — need split invoicing & revrec confirmation

Hi Jordan / Dylan,

Quick finance note from our side — thanks for flagging.

Confirming Dylan's summary: Redwood recognizes revenue over the period services are delivered (ASC 606 — transfer of service over time). How we invoice you does not change revenue recognition; the accounting treatment is driven by contract and service period.

Operational details we need to capture to support your auditors:
- Signed contract showing total committed consideration and coverage dates.
- Billing instructions: billing address, PO number(s), GL codes, and whether FinTrust requires separate vendor IDs per fiscal year.
- For Option A (single upfront payment with allocation invoices): we'll book received cash to a deferred revenue liability account and amortize monthly; we can provide a revrec schedule in CSV that maps months -> recognized revenue for your audit team.

Journal entries (simplified):
- On payment: Dr Cash / Cr Deferred Revenue
- Monthly: Dr Deferred Revenue / Cr Subscription Revenue

If you require separate invoices for FY26/FY27/FY28 (for your AP workflow), we can issue three invoices that reference one contract and one payment, or we can issue three invoices tied to three POs — whichever your procurement prefers. Note: separate POs increase operational overhead for both sides.

Attachments I'm sharing: FT-2312_revrec_memo.pdf (one-pager) and a sample billing_schedule.xlsx with line-level mapping. Neha — please add the draft SOW and the discount language we're offering for the full prepay.

Regards,
Karthik
VP, Finance
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@fintrust.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prepay billing — need split invoicing & revrec confirmation

Thanks Karthik — that helps.

A couple of quick clarifications from FinTrust:
- We can sign a single contract, but we need invoices dated 06/30/2026 (FY26), 06/30/2027 (FY27), and 06/30/2028 (FY28). Can Redwood backdate allocation invoices to those dates for matching? If not, we need invoices issued before close that reference the FY allocation.
- Second, would Redwood consider increasing the full-prepay discount from 6% to 10% if we do immediate full payment? Our procurement has flexibility on timing if the economics improve.
- Lastly, will Redwood provide the SOC2 evidence and the revrec memo in a single package for our internal audit? That would speed our approval.

Jordan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@fintrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-13T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prepay billing — need split invoicing & revrec confirmation

Jordan —

Appreciate the specifics. Quick answers and next steps:

- Invoices: We cannot legally backdate invoices, but we can issue allocation invoices dated on or before 06/30/2026 that reference the FY allocation (e.g., Invoice A dated 06/29/2026 for FY26 allocation). That should satisfy your AP cutoff.

- Discount: I ran this with Finance and we can move to 9% for immediate full payment; 10% is at director approval. If you can confirm immediate payment on receipt of DocuSign, I will escalate to request the final 10% approval. Neha — please prepare a one-line amendment option for DocuSign showing 9% and an approvable path to 10% pending leadership sign-off.

- SOC2 + RevRec package: Karthik will bundle the revrec memo and a redacted SOC2 evidence packet into one PDF for your auditors. We'll include the journal mapping and a contact for SOC2 evidence requests.

Next step: I'll send a 30-min invite with Karthik and your controller. If you can send the PO(s) and billing address ahead of that call, we'll prepare the invoices and the DocuSign package.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Dylan
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: FT-2312_billing_schedule.xlsx (proposed allocations), FT-2312_revrec_memo.pdf, FT-2312_draft_sow.docx
